name: High-Energy Plasma

VINIT.justification: Pre-ionized neutral matter with zero conductivity and zero collective behavior.

TANCH.justification: The operational ceiling where kinetic pressure equals magnetic pressure, defining containment stability.

AFWD.justification: Linear transformation of electromagnetic energy into kinetic energy, increasing plasma temperature.

AREV.justification: Energy loss through photon emission during ion-electron collisions, cooling the system.

CLINK.justification: Sequential transport of particles across magnetic field lines, linking core state to edge behavior.

IMSCRIB.justification: The plasma's internal recognition and neutralization of its own electric fields, maintaining quasi-neutrality.

FSPLIT.justification: A neutral atom branches into a distinct free electron and a positive ion.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of a neutral atom from a free electron and a positive ion.

EVALT.justification: High-confinement regime achieved via edge transport barrier formation.

EVALF.justification: Sudden loss of confinement and termination of the plasma state.

ENGAGR.justification: A periodic instability where the plasma is simultaneously confined and leaking, held in cyclic tension.

IFIX.justification: Permanent, irreversible physical record of plasma-wall interactions on the vessel lining.

steps.domain_action: Neutral gas injection into the vacuum vessel
Application of external RF voltage for breakdown
Ionization begins, separating neutrals into charged ions and electrons
Formation of the Debye sheath, self-recognizing the boundary potential
Development of the toroidal current via transformer induction
Ohmic heating increases particle kinetic energy
Full ionization sweep, removing all remaining neutral particles
Reaching the H-mode threshold with steep pressure gradients
Initiation of ELM cycles, preserving the pedestal through periodic bursts
Radiative cooling via impurities in the plasma edge
Accidental recombination during edge-localized cooling events
Transport of heat to the divertor targets
Deposition of tritium into the beryllium first-wall tiles
Reaching the Greenwald density limit for maximum operating capacity

phase_5.compiler_frontend: External magnetic coil controllers acting on the MHD equilibrium
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Magnetic field configuration and flux surface topology

phase_6.cycle_cost: External power injection (MW) subtracted by radiation loss
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The Frobenius cycle of ionization and recombination is structurally conservative for the particle identities.
